discovery: Conformal field theory of two-dimensional critical phenomena

nominees.name: Alexander A. Belavin
nominees.affiliation: Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics, Russia

motivation: In 1984 Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov showed that at a critical point in two dimensions, scale invariance extends to the infinite-dimensional conformal symmetry, and that this symmetry fixes the theory. Their minimal models give exact critical exponents and correlation functions for the Ising, Potts, tricritical and other universality classes. They are a rare case of a problem that is simple to state and has an exact solution. This work, together with Polyakov's earlier ideas on conformal invariance and Zamolodchikov's c-theorem and integrable field theories, changed how we understand phase transitions, the renormalization group and universality. It has been confirmed by numerics and experiments on two-dimensional systems, and today it underpins the physics of quantum spin chains, the edge states of the fractional quantum Hall effect, surface growth and string theory. It is also a strong example of fundamental theory later finding uses nobody expected.
